dedupe_keys.name: openlain5g reproducible 4g lte and 5g sa network laboratory framework

description: OpenLain5G is a modular framework, written by Willian Roy Canazas Rosas, Manuel Ismael Prieto Tito and Alberth Ronal Tamo Calla, for reproducible 4G LTE and 5G standalone mobile network laboratories. It deploys and manages open-source radio access, core, IMS and simulation components, including Open5GS, srsRAN and UERANSIM, through Docker Compose, a command-line tool and a web application, with four public profiles, declarative configuration, automated validation and traceable evidence of each run. Software-only scenarios need no radio hardware; guarded workflows for Ettus X-Series USRP radios stay fail-closed until transmission is separately authorised. Coverage: a laboratory network on one GNU/Linux host, not a real deployment. Format and access: source on GitHub under the MIT licence, archived on Zenodo (v1.1.5, August 2026) with English and Spanish documentation; the installer provisions Docker and the images. Caveats: a young project from a small team; results reflect open-source stacks, not vendor equipment; radio experiments need a spectrum licence. Simulation uses: emulated mobile networks for digital twin experiments, testing core and RAN failure and recovery procedures, and teaching. Related records: Mininet and GNS3 emulate IP networks, Simu5G and ns-3 simulate 5G, and NVIDIA AODT is a commercial RAN digital twin.
